title: What do you use for sprites/assets without hitting limits or paying?
author: Any-Landscape434
selftext:
Just wondering if its possible to make art with ai or if it should be avoided? What do you all do for art if you got no money and no art skills?

Ive wanted to make a game but i always talk myself out of starting.

But for images, i just used codex (again, simplicty is king for me). for music and sounds im actually programing it using [strudel.cc](http://strudel.cc) (a modified version i recently made with a DAW and freq visualizer.

comments.author: AsparagusOk8818
comments.body:
Um. For $0? 

...I am reasonably confident you could create an ASCII game with ChatGPT just using the free chat. It would not be Agentic, you'd have to copy/paste the code yourself, probably there's going to be context limits and other problems. But a simple ASCII dungeon crawler or something like that is, probably, possible for free. 

A game with actual art assets and agentic coding? No shot. You can't do that for free. 

My own minimalist coding set-up is the $20/month ChatGPT plan, using mostly Sol and sometimes Astra. It works fine for a game of reasonably high complexity. 

For art, I also pay for Sprite Fusion's pixel art services ($20/month). ChatGPT's imagegen is, at the moment, unsuitable in terms of quality. MOSS Turbo + a LoRA can also work locally and for free to generate pixel art, but the quality will be a bit lower. 

Some people will cite Tripo or Meshy. These services are not useful unless you are already a 3D modeler, and cannot currently create either good animations or models that can animate well. 

  
So, you need a minimum of $20-$40\~ per month, more than that if you also want to make music for the game.

comments.author: ValhallaSun
comments.body: I’ve been developing a browser-based MMORPG for two years. I only started because ChatGPT began generating images. comments.body:
https://i.redd.it/18qp44zbg12i1.gif

I make my own muahahahahah.  althoguh to be fair,  the components in that test render are from a sheet I made on gemini.  I just said, hey give me a sprite sheet with a greenscreen background, make them all flat graphics no shading on angling, sci fi solder parts such as limbs, feet and weapons.

then I used my own home brew animation studio to split out all my sprites from the sprite sheet and my skeletal animation thing to stick them on a skeleton and then animate them! MUAHHAHAH!.

If you wanna do this stuff for free, like really.

learn how to use comfyui,  with a local model the only limit is your time to generate stuff and your graphics card.

ill also add the ai can make graphics,  you just gotta teach it how to do it really. they can draw shapes, pixels, lines, all kindsa stuff so really it can prodecurally make a buncha assets, just gotta tell it to do it.

comments.author: dtlater
comments.body:
Mileage may vary but nearly all my assets have been generated with free image models in ComfyUI.

I have a bunch of CC sessions, and one is dedicated only to generate and select the best assets. If a coding agent needs art it's instructed to negotiate what's needed from the asset agent and that'll go off and try generating it while the coding agent does something else. I've been time boxing my projects so they aren't perfect (some may say they're not even good) but it's saved a fortune over relying on foundational models.

These are two different style games, but both shared the exact same asset agent orchestrating different comfy workflows.

[2d sidescroller](https://omniu.itch.io/atom-scouts-nebula-demo)

[3d flight sim](https://omniu.itch.io/atom-scouts-crossfire-demo)

replies.author: VoidMechDev
replies.body: And you pay for ComfyUI Cloud? or you have an inference provider?

replies.author: dtlater
replies.body:
No, everything runs locally on my own PC, so there's no cloud subscription. Speed and quality depend on your hardware.

I use a few free open models: one for creating and editing images, one for animating images into video (that's how I make sprite sheets), one for turning images into 3D models, and one for game music. I used to learn model names and create the workflows but now it can kinda select what would work best for me. 

Blender is also free, and CC can use it to clean up and texture the 3D models and that's worked better than like meshy for my purposes.

comments.author: Mrbuttshaman
comments.body: Just ask Claude.  It will tell you.  That said, easiest to have Claude make you a 3d poseable mannequin, have it use comfy UI to generate concept art and use trellis to create character models, then pose them and ask Claude to use an image to image generation tool in comfy UI to make sprites for the poses using the references.  I have also tried nano banana 2 and you can get really far with asking it for sprite sheets but if you have a lot that you need they can start drifting in a way that you might never recover from.  If you have some body tracking you can also act out some things and let it make sprites from your clips with the 3d models.  I had Claude make me motion capture software and plugins for blender and krita to make the whole process smoother for me.

comments.author: CycleMother2006
comments.body:
Quixel megascans is literally free. 40,000 or something realistic models, though you'd probably need to use with Unreal since they're fairly demanding in polys for a non-nanite engine.

Alternatively go watch a few tutorials on making low poly assets in Blender. Imphenzia can knock out a prop in like 30 seconds. You can then also pick up a multitude of free low poly asset packs that are out there in the various sites/libraries to cover some of the basics.

If 2D, then you need an image gen, free or otherwise, or the easiest alternative is probably learning how to draw very simple sprites in something like libresprite or an alternative. Anyone can do pixel art. An alternative style would be something like Cult of the Lamb style. You don't have to be some incredible artist to make interesting sprites/assets. I was drawing Cult of the Lamb equivalents in a notebook in elementary school, and I wouldn't have called myself talented or anything of the sort.  That style is very simple to animate, too and very reusable. It just draws everything in parts. The heads are a part, each arm piece is a part, etc. All of which are just very basic primitive shapes. Highly recommend for aspiring 2d devs that want a consistent style and have a game that is remotely cozy in theme if they don't have some other way to produce reliably good looking designs.
